data.content_ref: inline:The problem asks specifically what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer. SRC_001's evidence-of-gain criterion — 'detection of basic errors that experts habitually overlook' — is exactly the ambiguity the problem demands be resolved: catching trivial errors is consistent with both a genuine reliability improvement AND rote checklist compliance that merely happens to land on the right answer without deeper understanding. The target offers no within-evaluation probe (e.g., performance on novel items where the checklist does not map, or error-pattern analysis separating mechanistic tick-box agreement from substantive judgment) to separate these. It thus answers the evidence-distinguishing half of the problem by restating the very phenomenon to be distinguished.
